steps.message:
# Consolidate heterogeneous bank statement parsers

The bank-statement subsystem has accumulated duplicated parsing paths for individual institutions. Consolidate the common PDF-to-table behavior so the shared bank parser handles the overlapping formats used by Andhra Bank, Bank of Baroda, City Union Bank, HSBC, Karur Vysya, Kotak, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab National Bank, and the existing generic consumers. Keep truly bank-specific fallbacks only where their formats still require them.

The shared parser must remain tolerant of real statement noise. Month-name dates may contain spaces, optional hyphens, or no separators; normalize them consistently, including the known `JUY` OCR error for July. Recognize opening-balance and repeated transaction-header rows, retain a dated transaction even when its description cell is blank, and preserve transaction date, description, debit or credit direction, amount, and running balance across both supported multi-line HTML layouts. A balance-bearing continuation row without its own date inherits the preceding transaction date rather than disappearing.

Update the bank service adapters to send compatible statement layouts through the shared parser. Andhra's `WHERE INDIA BANKS` layout keeps its regex-specific path, Bank of Baroda's statement-criteria layout uses the description-above-date path, its other compatible layouts use the description-below-date path, and its distinct saving-account layout must continue using the existing dedicated parser. Consolidate common basic-detail extraction without regressing bank-specific account-holder rules.

Do not add real bank statements, customer data, cloud credentials, or production endpoints to the repository. The task must work against synthetic fixtures and preserve the behavior of unaffected formats.

Verify with:

    cd /app && sh /tests/test.sh
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase.

131:     public static String dateRegexFromString(String date) {
132:         if (date.find("([0-3]?[0-9] [A-z]{3,4} [0-9]{2,4})")) {
133:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9] [A-z]{3,4} [0-9]{2,4})\$"
134:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
135:             return "[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}"
136:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM)))")) {
137:             return "[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}"
138:         } else if (date.find("[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")) {
139:             return "^[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}\$"
140:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")) {
141:             return "^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}\$"
142:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}")) {
143:             return "^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}\$"
144:         } else if (date.find("[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{2}")) {
145:             return "^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{2}\$"
146:         } else if (date.find("([0-3]?[0-9]-[\\s]*[A-z]{3,4}-[\\s]*[0-9]{2,4})")) {
147:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9]-[A-z]{3,4}-[0-9]{2,4})\$"
148:         } else if (date.find("[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-3]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4}")) {
149:             return "(^[0-1]?[0-9]/[0-3]?[0-9]/[0-9]{4})\$"
150:         } else if (date.find("[0-3]?[0-9]-[0-1]?[0-9]-[0-9]{2}")) {
151:             return "(^[0-3]?[0-9]-[0-1]?[0-9]-[0-9]{2})\$"
152:         }
153:     }

155:     public static String processValue(String headerValue) {
156:         if (headerValue.length() == 1 && headerValue.find("-")) {
157:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("-", "")
158:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
159:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
160:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
161:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
162:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}[\\s]*-?[0-9]*[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|([0-1]?[0-9]:[0-6][0-9]))")) {
163:             headerValue = headerValue.find("[0-3][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-9]{4}")
164:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[0-9]{4}[\\s]*(([0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9][\\s]*(AM|PM))|(([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-6][0-9]))")) {
165:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("[\\s]*[0-1][0-9]:[0-6][0-9]:[0-6][0-9] (AM|PM)", "").replaceAll("[\\s]*([0-1]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-6][0-9]", "")
166:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]/[0-1][0-9]/[\\s]*[0-9]{4}")) {
167:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll(" ", "")
168:         } else if (headerValue.find("^[0-3][0-9]-[A-Z][a-z]{2}-[0-9]{4} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}")) {
169:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}", "").trim()
170:         } else if (headerValue.find("([0-3]?[0-9]-[\\s]*[A-z]{3,4}-[\\s]*[0-9]{2,4})")) {
171:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll(" ", "").trim()
172:         } else if (headerValue.find("^-\$")) {
173:             headerValue = headerValue.replaceAll("-", "").trim()
174:         }
175:         return headerValue
176:     }

steps.message:
I've completed the consolidation. Summary of the work:

## Shared parser hardening — `src/groovy/com/bankScraper/bank/BankTransactionUtil.groovy`

New reusable primitives (used by every table-based path):
- `normalizeDate` / `parseDate(String[, pattern])` (BankTransactionUtil.groovy:196, :221) — month-name dates with spaces, hyphens/slashes/dots or **no separator** (`12JAN2016`, `1-Feb-16`, `03 / mar / 2016`) all normalize to one representation; the `JUY` OCR error maps to `JUL`. `parseDate` returns `null` instead of throwing, so callers decide how to treat a row. Numeric formats (`dd/MM/yyyy`, `dd-MM-yy`, `yyyy-MM-dd`, …) are untouched.
- `isTransactionHeaderRow`, `isJunkRow`, `isOpeningBalanceRow` (case-insensitive `B/F` / `OPENING BALANCE` / `BALANCE BROUGHT FORWARD`), `whetherDescriptionContinuationRow`, `isCompleteAmount`, `cellText`, `assignAmountAndType` — the duplicated debit/credit/amount/indicator handling now lives in one place.
- Header dictionary gained case-tolerant, anchored variants (`Transaction details`, `Additional narrative`, `Dr/Cr`, …) — verified index detection is byte-identical for 14 legacy header rows and only *adds* previously-missed description/amount-type columns.

Behaviour in both multi-line layouts (`…DescriptionAboveDate`, `…DescriptionBelowDate`):
- repeated mid-table headers and total/closing rows are skipped instead of raising parse failures;
- opening-balance rows are recognised and not emitted as transactions;
- a dated row with a **blank description** is retained;
- a **balance-bearing row without a date** becomes its own transaction, inheriting the date of the preceding dated row (or preceding transaction) rather than disappearing — while a *fragmented* balance (wrapped over two lines) is still merged as a continuation;
- date, description, debit/credit direction, amount, balance, value date and cheque remark are preserved.

## Service adapters
- `AndhraBankPdfService` — `WHERE INDIA BANKS` keeps `AndhraBankUtil.extractTransactionsFromCurrentAccount`; every other layout goes through the shared description-below-date path.
- `BankOfBarodaPdfService` — statement-criteria layout → description-**above**-date; other compatible layouts → description-**below**-date; the distinct `Joint Holders`/`PARTICULARS` saving layout still uses `BankOfBarodaUtil.extractTransactionsFromSavingAccount`.
- `HsbcPdfService` — `Additional narrative` → below-date, otherwise above-date.
- `KarurVysyaPdfService` — `Account Activity` → above-date (TODO resolved).
- `OrientalBankOfCommercePdfService` → below-date.
- Kotak/City Union/PNB already feed the shared parser for their compatible layouts; their genuinely single-column/regex formats keep their dedicated fallbacks.

## Basic details
`CityUnionBankUtil.extractAccountHolderName` and `HSBCBankUtil.extractAccountHolderName` added and registered in `BankUtil.getAccountHolderName`, so the common `BankUtil.extractBasicInformation` path yields the right holder for those banks without changing any bank-specific rule.

## Verification note
`/tests/test.sh` does not exist in this container, so I could not run the stated command. Instead I validated out-of-repo (`/tmp/opencode/h`, nothing added to the repo) with the bundled Grails 2.3.11 Groovy compiler: all 183 repo sources still parse, `BankTransactionUtil` compiles, synthetic fixtures exercise each requirement above, and a differential old-vs-new run over classic single/multi-page, numeric-date, wrapped-balance, reverse-order and JSON-path fixtures shows **no behavioural regressions** — the only diffs are the intended fixes. No statements, customer data, credentials or endpoints were added.
